# Fresh native MOSDBackoff vectors

Ceph v20.2.4 commit `7f793731f1b39eb4f465e960113d2363c311b964`.
Generated by the independent development wrapper
`tools/osd_backoff_native_encoder.cc` and driver
`tools/osd_backoff_native_encoder.py` on 2026-10-15.

The five logical messages are independently constructed in C++: one binary
single-object BLOCK, one half-open BLOCK, its original-epoch ACK_BLOCK, a
newer-epoch UNBLOCK, and a sharded PG with global minimum/maximum bounds.
Fresh native `encode_payload` produces every front. A separately allocated
native decoder checks PG, shard, epoch, opcode, full uint64 ID and both hobjects.
Decoded objects are never passed back to an encoder. The wrapper has no network
connection and consumes no Go-produced bytes or captured socket data.

All messages use type 61, version 1/compatibility 1, TID zero and priority 127.
The explicit offline inputs sequence 1 and ACK sequence 3 are projected from
the native Message envelope into the native `ceph_msg_header2`/MessageFrame API.
This proves native envelope serialization, not ProtocolV2 session execution,
server-generated BLOCK/UNBLOCK, protocol ACK delivery or feature acceptance.

`backoff-native-provenance.json` records pinned source and submodule hashes,
wrapper/driver hashes, the actual matching native library loader audit, binary
hash, generated configuration hash, per-segment hashes, native header metadata
and independently decoded control receipts. The owned builder termination is
confirmed in that manifest.

`TestBackoffMatchesFreshNativeEncoder` passes Go encoder/header equality and
native output decoding for all five messages, including ACK equality with the
independently constructed native ACK vector. Dedicated fixture-harness tests
reject controls disguised as operations/replies/watch events, wrong versions,
nonzero TID, nonempty data, and missing/inconsistent decoder provenance. Existing
operation and watch16 provenance tests continue to pass.

The native builder cache must not be used by concurrent compiler runs. Product
Go builds and runtime do not depend on these native tools or generated files.
